title: Virtual communication: pros & cons
blurb: Outline the advantages and disadvantages of email, video and phone conferencing, messaging and collaboration tools.
question: A payroll upgrade team works from Glasgow, Manila and Austin and communicates almost entirely by email, video calls and a shared collaboration tool. What does virtual communication make possible for them, and what problems should the project manager expect?

teach.body: Virtual communication uses technology to connect people who are not in the same place: email, video and phone conferencing, instant messaging, collaboration tools and shared workspaces, the intranet and social media. In plain English: if it reaches people through a screen, a headset or a phone, it is virtual. A cameras-on video call is still virtual, not face to face.

Virtual methods are fast and reach dispersed teams and large audiences at once, wherever people are, so a project can draw on people and skills from anywhere. They are low cost (no travel) and convenient. Many are flexible: people can contribute asynchronously, at a time that suits their time zone. Most written tools (email, messaging, shared documents) also create a record automatically.

teach.body: Fiona's team is spread across Glasgow, Manila and Austin. A collaboration tool lets each site post updates in its own working day, and email gives a written trail of decisions. A weekly video call means faces are seen without anyone flying. But the call lands late in the evening for Manila, a network outage wipes out one review, and a terse email from Austin is read as criticism in Glasgow.

teach.h: One live call, three local times (winter)
teach.caption: Live virtual meetings across time zones push someone outside normal hours. Asynchronous tools avoid this.

teach.text: Virtual communication has FEWER non-verbal cues than face to face, so options claiming it 'gives the richest body language' or 'makes conflict easy to spot' are wrong. And it DOES depend on technology: that is a virtual disadvantage, never a physical one.

items: Virtual = through technology: email, video and phone conferencing, messaging, collaboration tools, intranet, social media.
Advantages: fast, reaches dispersed teams and many people, low cost, convenient, flexible (asynchronous), often creates a record.
Disadvantages: depends on technology, fewer non-verbal cues, overload, misinterpretation, security risks, harder to build trust, time zones, can exclude some.
A video call is virtual, not face to face.

summary: You can now recognise virtual communication and outline its advantages (speed, reach, low cost, convenience, asynchronous flexibility, a built-in record) and its disadvantages (technology dependence, fewer cues, overload, misinterpretation, security, trust, time zones and exclusion).

A.q: Which of the following is an advantage of virtual communication?
options: It gives the richest non-verbal cues
A.why: Virtual tools connect people wherever they are, quickly and without travel, which is ideal for dispersed teams.

whyNot.0: Face to face gives the richest cues; virtual methods give fewer.
whyNot.1: Virtual communication depends on technology by definition.
whyNot.3: No method guarantees understanding; feedback is still needed.

A.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of using email on a project?
options: It leaves no written trail of decisions
Tone can be misread without vocal cues
It can only reach one person at a time
It is slow compared with posting a letter
A.why: Email carries words only, so a short or firm message can be read as rude or hostile, and the reader cannot see the sender's intent.

whyNot.0: Email creates a written trail, which is an advantage.
whyNot.2: Email can go to many recipients at once.
whyNot.3: Email is far faster than posting a letter.

A.q: Which of the following is an example of virtual communication?
options: A workshop held in the boardroom
A poster in the staff canteen
A video conference with a supplier
A.why: A video conference connects people through technology, so it is virtual even though faces are visible.

whyNot.0: A workshop in the boardroom is face to face.
whyNot.2: A printed newsletter is physical communication.

B.q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of virtual communication?
options: Contributions can be made at any time
Many people can be reached at once
Trust is built faster than in person
B.why: Building trust and rapport is harder virtually; it is a recognised disadvantage, not an advantage.

whyNot.0: Asynchronous working is a key virtual advantage.
whyNot.1: Avoiding travel is why virtual methods are low cost.
whyNot.2: Wide, fast reach is a core virtual advantage.

B.q: A project moves all reviews onto a new collaboration tool. Several site supervisors have no licence and have never used it, so they miss key decisions. Which disadvantage does this show?
options: It needs access and skills some people lack
It provides too much non-verbal information
It is slow to print and distribute updates
It creates a record that cannot be changed
B.why: Virtual tools depend on people having access and the skills to use them; without both, some stakeholders are excluded.

whyNot.1: Virtual tools give fewer non-verbal cues, not more.
whyNot.2: Printing and distribution are physical disadvantages.
whyNot.3: A record is an advantage, and it is not what caused the problem.

B.q: Team members in four countries add comments to a shared plan on an online tool, each during their own working day. Which advantage of virtual communication does this show?
options: It removes the need for any record
B.why: Asynchronous working means people contribute at different times, which suits dispersed teams in different time zones.

whyNot.1: Comments on a shared plan carry no body language.
whyNot.2: Shared tools usually create a record; removing it is not the benefit.
whyNot.3: An online tool depends on technology.

C.q: Which TWO are disadvantages of virtual communication? 1) Information overload. 2) Security risks to data. 3) High travel costs. 4) No record is ever created.
C.why: Virtual channels make it easy to send too much (overload), and data sent electronically can be exposed or misdirected (security).

whyNot.1: Statement 3 is wrong: virtual methods avoid travel costs.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is wrong: many virtual tools create a record automatically.
whyNot.3: Both are wrong: no travel is needed, and records are often created.

C.q: A team spread across the UK, India and the US holds a live video call every morning UK time. Which disadvantage is most likely to arise?
options: Faces cannot be seen on the call
Some must join outside working hours
The call leaves a permanent paper trail
C.why: Live virtual sessions across time zones force some members to join very early or very late.

whyNot.0: A video call does show faces, though with fewer cues than in person.
whyNot.1: Virtual calls remove the need to travel.
whyNot.3: A call creates no paper trail, and a record would be an advantage anyway.

C.q: A team member emails a spreadsheet of supplier bank details to the wrong external address. Which disadvantage of virtual communication does this illustrate?
C.why: Electronic information can be sent to the wrong place or intercepted in seconds, a security risk of virtual methods.

whyNot.0: Nothing was printed or delivered; this is a physical drawback.
whyNot.2: Missing cues cause misunderstanding, not a data leak.
whyNot.3: Virtual methods reach many people easily; that is an advantage.

reteach.title: The family group chat
reteach.question: A family spread across three countries plans a big birthday through a group chat and video calls. What works, and what goes wrong?

blocks.h: Planning a party from three countries
blocks.body: The group chat means everyone can join in, for free, whenever they are awake, and the plan is written down for all to scroll back through. A video call lets Grandma see everyone. But the chat hits 300 messages and someone misses the venue change, a short reply ('fine.') is read as sulking, Grandma's internet keeps dropping, and the only call time that works is midnight for the cousins in Sydney.

blocks.text: Every item in the 'goes wrong' column has a project name: time zones, information overload, misinterpretation and technology dependence.

explain.body: Virtual means communicating through technology: email, video and phone conferencing, instant messaging, collaboration tools, the intranet and social media. A phone conference counts as virtual too, because it relies on technology to connect people who are apart.

explain.h: Virtual, from most to least written

test.q: In the PFQ's three groupings, a phone conference with the supplier is classed as which method?
test.why: A phone conference connects people through technology, so it is a virtual method.

whyNot.0: Face to face needs people physically together.
whyNot.1: Physical communication is tangible or printed.
whyNot.3: Informal is a style of communication, not one of the three methods.

explain.h: Advantage: speed, reach and low cost
explain.body: One email or video call reaches people in many locations at once, with no travel. That makes virtual methods fast, convenient and cheap, and lets a project use people based anywhere.

items.label: seconds to send, minutes to gather
reaches every site and many people

test.q: What is the main reason virtual communication is cost-effective for a dispersed project team?
options: No travel is needed to take part
No technology needs to be bought
Fewer messages need to be sent
test.why: People take part from wherever they are, so travel and venue costs are avoided.

whyNot.1: Virtual communication relies on technology, which has its own cost.
whyNot.2: Virtual channels often increase message volume, not reduce it.
whyNot.3: Virtual meetings still need agendas to be effective.

explain.body: Asynchronous tools such as email and shared workspaces let people contribute when it suits them, across time zones. Written virtual tools also keep a record of what was said and decided, which helps later.

explain.h: One shared document, three working days

test.q: Which virtual tool best lets team members contribute at different times of day?
test.why: A shared collaboration space is asynchronous: each person can add to it whenever they are working.

whyNot.0: A live video conference needs everyone at the same time.
whyNot.1: A live phone conference also needs everyone at the same time.
whyNot.2: A live presentation is synchronous; people must attend when it runs.

explain.body: Virtual communication depends on technology (failures, access, skills), carries fewer non-verbal cues so messages are misread, encourages information overload, brings security risks, makes trust harder to build, creates time-zone clashes and can exclude people.

test.q: Project staff receive over 100 emails a day and a key change notice goes unread. Which disadvantage of virtual communication is this?
test.why: Virtual channels make sending easy, so the volume grows until important messages are lost.

whyNot.0: Email creates a written record; the problem was volume.
whyNot.3: Email is delivered instantly; it was read too late, or not at all, because of volume.
